conviction_note: One small sourced negative: crude has run well above the $80 Jul-Mar assumption set at Q1. With a sensitivity of -12.1億円 per $1 JCC, the headline (time-lag-inclusive) FY guide is under pressure at this H1 print. But the input is public, analysts have started cutting (Q2 EPS 95.3 to 70.9 within the last 7 days), the company steers on ex-time-lag profit, which rises with crude through upstream, and no capital-return lever is set up the way last year's H1 DOE raise was (+8.75%). So the findings sum to -0.3, and the scaled number is a near-coin-flip at p_up 48 on a 2.3% scale.

findings.finding: Crude has run well above the $80/bbl JCC (and ¥160/$) Jul-Mar assumption that Osaka Gas set at Q1. Brent was $95.63 on 2026-09-02 and about $102 in early October, WTI $100-102 around 10-19/20, and Dubai averaged ¥14,593/bbl in September (about $92). The company's own sensitivity is -12.1億円 of time-lag-inclusive ordinary profit per +$1 (and -6.2億円 per ¥1 weaker yen). Resetting the assumption at this H1 print implies roughly -¥10-20bn of extra time-lag loss against the ¥190bn guide. This is partly offset by the yen at ~¥158 (+¥1bn) and by ex-time-lag gains (overseas upstream, LNG contract competitiveness, power prices), which the Q1 deck showed the company using to hold the headline guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026-07-30, 14:00 release: crude assumption lifted $65 to $80, ¥14bn time-lag loss absorbed, headline guide held and ex-time-lag raised. The stock went 5,616 to 5,519 (-1.7%) that day and was flat the next (Yahoo chart). H1 2025-10-30: forecast raised plus the DOE 3.0% to 3.5% policy change and dividend 105 to 120; the next session was +8.75% (baseline history).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The crude path is public daily and one analyst has already cut Q2 EPS from 95.3 to 70.9. But the FY consensus (384.57, 5 analysts) still sits at or above the company's 380.73. That is what it would look like if most of the street were waiting for the company's new assumption before cutting the time-lag-inclusive line. If this were fully priced, the FY consensus would sit visibly below plan. The stock has instead risen from ~5,400 in August to 5,876.
findings.independence: Crude levels come from separate sources: kumanichi/Kyodo WTI 101.79 on 10-20 (https://kumanichi.com/articles/2048818), pps-net Dubai Sep average ¥14,593/bbl (https://pps-net.org/statistics/crude-oil2), and Brent 95.63 on 2026-09-02 (customs/market summary via search). The sensitivity and the assumption both come from one company document, so this is one finding.

findings.finding: No capital-return catalyst is set up the way it was last year. The FY2027.3 dividend of ¥130 (65+65) was pre-announced on 2026-03-13 and already implies DOE of 3.7% against the 3.5% policy. The ¥80bn buyback (28m shares, to 2027-03-31) is running on pace, at ¥35.2bn / 6.31m shares by 2026-09-30. So the H1 lever that produced last year's +8.75% (the DOE 3.0% to 3.5% raise and dividend 105 to 120 at the 2025-10-30 H1) is not obviously available. A further 増配 or buyback would be a surprise, not a base case.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-10-30 H1: DOE policy raise plus 増配 and a forecast raise gave +8.75% the next session. Since then the returns have been pre-announced (2026-03-13 dividend plan, 2026-05-08 buyback) and have not landed at a quarterly print.
findings.why_not_priced: Sized 0: the pre-announced returns are fully public. The finding lowers the odds of a last-year-style upside surprise rather than adding a direction. The right tail is in impact_high.

bar_hierarchy: Forecast revision: likely. The crude assumption ($80 JCC) is stale against ~$92-102 crude, so the time-lag-inclusive guide is at risk and ex-time-lag is likely up. The net direction against a street that sits at plan leans slightly negative. Returns: none expected (¥130 dividend pre-announced at DOE 3.7%; the ¥80bn buyback is 44% done); last year's H1 policy raise is the upside tail. New-year guide: not applicable at H1 (the new mid-term plan comes in March). Quarter: H1 time-lag-inclusive ordinary will fall well below last year's ¥105.5bn, which carried time-lag gains, so progress against ¥190bn will look low (~40-45% against last year's 57%), but that is mechanical and visible.

baseline_tension: The priced lean is -0.37 (mostly margin overhang at 3.32x) and the run-up is a mild +2.2%. My small negative agrees with the lean, so it adds little. The strongest positive the release could carry is the Q1 pattern repeated: time-lag-inclusive guide held, ex-time-lag raised again on upstream and LNG competitiveness, plus a dividend nudge in line with last year's H1 policy move. I looked for it; nothing pre-signals it, and it is why p_up stays near 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a negative resting on a series the market already has): the crude finding rests on public daily prices, so it moves from -0.4 to -0.3 and p_up from 47 to 48. It is kept because the release can ADD the forecast reset itself.
Rule 2 (check the sign): the strongest positive (held headline guide plus a higher ex-time-lag guide, and a returns surprise) is written in baseline_tension; it was looked for, so nothing else moves.
